captions.facebook:
FINANCIAL EDUCATION · Education edition

Financial resilience starts with a buffer

A financial buffer is money set aside for the unexpected: a car repair, a medical bill, a gap between jobs.

Without one, a surprise cost often goes on a credit card or a loan, and interest makes it bigger.

Many educators describe the buffer in months of essential expenses rather than as a dollar figure, because every household's costs are different.

Building it slowly from existing income still counts. Consistency matters more than size.

A buffer is one way of planning ahead, so a surprise stays manageable.

Are you financially ready for tomorrow?

Knowing your essential monthly costs is where preparedness begins.

Learn. Understand. Stay Informed.
